problem.text: The CLI chat loop lacked commands to retry or edit replies, change the system prompt and banned strings, or persist conversation state.

reasoning.text: The change extends the existing command dispatcher and keeps edits in local session state. Reply editing requires coordinated changes to input prefilling, prompt tokenization and output accumulation; these are not independent conveniences.

impact.text: Users gain /r, /e, /sp, /ban, /save and /load without reloading the model. Source inspection also identifies unguarded empty-history commands and an explicit-filename /load path that does not load anything.

source_notes.text: Read ancestor entry 769ddb34b02769e9a8189d4f4b9653784f2516ba. It establishes the earlier runtime command/input interface and records a nonpositive code-block-index defect.
The earlier /cc defect is carried over: the task leaves its dispatch unchanged, and the parent helper still clamps only indices greater than the number of blocks.

Closed discussions #6, “No ROCm runtime is found, using ROCM_HOME='/usr'”; #12, “Qwen2.5 Coder 0.5B Instruct | ValueError: Unsupported type in stop_conditions”; #39, “Gemma 3 architecture not in list?”; #43, “Error converting abliterated Qwen3 mlabonne/Qwen3-30B-A3B-abliterated”; and PR #22, “OpenAI compatible API example”, concern startup, template selection, architecture availability, conversion and API hosting respectively. Any relationship to this task is inferred from their references to chat.py, not an upstream link to these commands.

Unreferenced #52, “Error converting moonshotai/Kimi-Dev-72B”, discusses conversion overflow and later recommends chat.py for template diagnosis. #48, “`RuntimeError` when requesting logprobs with Gemma 3 models”, reports a tensor-width mismatch in job.py. Their relevance is inferred only from shared inspected paths; neither establishes a motivation for this command change.

limitations: No interactive terminal, model generation, clipboard backend or filesystem save/load operation was executed. The successful Python check transcribed command control flow and exercised JSON in memory.
Literal whole-tree searches establish inspected repository call sites, not external or dynamically resolved consumers.
Session loading directly indexes JSON fields without schema validation; behavior for arbitrary malformed session contents was not exercised.

chapters.title: Editable replies and persistent chat sessions

claims.text: /r removes the last context pair and resubmits its user prompt. /e additionally opens the last reply as editable multiline input, then uses the edited text as an assistant prefix rather than a completed answer. Both proceed into the ordinary generation path.

read_input_ptk gains an optional prefix and passes it as prompt_toolkit's default text. Whole-parent searches found only chat.py selecting and calling this helper; both output modes select it. Existing three-argument input calls remain compatible, while /e, /sp and /ban supply a fourth argument. read_input_console and read_input_rich retain their old signatures but are not selected by this loop.

get_input_ids now receives a prefix argument at both its initial and trimming-loop calls. A nonempty prefix is appended after the formatted unanswered assistant turn and takes precedence over the automatic opening think tag. The prefix is also streamed before generated chunks. Streamer_basic accumulates it in all_text; Streamer_rich applies its existing reasoning/display state machine. The final context reply still comes from all_text.strip().

The previous stream call handled generated chunks inside an entered streamer context; the added prefix call uses the same context and think-tag arguments. Whole-tree stream-call search found no other Python chat-streamer callers. The existing reasoning-mode branch does not add thinking text to all_text, so prefix streaming is not unconditional preservation of every edited character.

/sp changes the system prompt for subsequent formatting without adding a turn. /ban edits one double-quoted string per line, discards unquoted lines and strips only the outer quotes; this is not JSON string decoding. Its status message reports the difference in list lengths, not a set difference. The initial list contains both think tags under --no_think, otherwise it is empty; subsequent Jobs receive the editable list.

Job's existing consumer lowercases nonempty banned-string lists and prepares UTF-32 buffers; an empty list takes the disabled branch. Thus the new empty-list default follows the same constructor branch as the former None default.

save_session writes system_prompt, banned_strings and context as indented UTF-8 JSON, after expanding ~ and requesting recursive creation of the parent directory. load_session uses the same path expansion and reads those exact fields. The default command filename is ~/chat_py_session.json. Model selection, sampler settings and the separate last-response variable are not part of this payload.

A bounded Python transcription showed that JSON turns become lists while remaining usable by the loop's append and whole-pair replacement operations. It also reproduced empty-history IndexError for /r and /e, and showed that /load saved.json bypasses both loading and the command-loop continue. These checks did not run the repository chat application.

findings.description: The /load implementation places loading and continue inside the no-filename branch.
findings.trigger: Enter /load saved.json in the interactive chat loop.
findings.expected_behavior: Read the requested session and return to command input without generating a response to the command.
findings.actual_behavior: len(c) is greater than one, so load_session is never called. Execution falls through to context.append and treats the command text as a user prompt.

verification.description: Compared the new match branch with the following context insertion and the script's main entry point. Both basic and rich output modes share this dispatcher.
Modeled the literal-space parser and conditional indentation for default and explicit-filename commands.
verification.limits: No file was opened and the repository main function did not run.

findings.description: Retry and edit assume a previous context pair without checking that one exists.
findings.trigger: Enter /r or /e immediately after startup, after /clear, or with --amnesia enabled.
findings.expected_behavior: Reject the command gracefully when there is no previous reply.
findings.actual_behavior: Both branches index context[-1] before any guard or exception handler and raise IndexError. --amnesia clears context before command input on every iteration.

verification.description: Inspected context initialization, amnesia clearing, /clear and both new branches in the shared CLI loop.
verification.limits: Reach is the inspected interactive main loop; external callers were not executed.

verification.description: Evaluated the branches' first context access on an empty list; both produced IndexError.

findings.description: The inherited code-block selector still accepts nonpositive indices without a lower bound.
findings.trigger: Enter /cc -2 after a response containing exactly two complete fenced code blocks.
findings.expected_behavior: Reject or normalize the invalid block number without terminating chat.
findings.actual_behavior: The helper evaluates matches[-num], yielding index 2 for a two-element list and raising IndexError. main catches integer-conversion failures only, not this helper failure.

verification.description: Whole-parent search located the helper definition and main's sole literal caller. Inspected both and verified that the task leaves this path unchanged.
verification.limits: No clipboard or interactive execution; the observation is carried over rather than introduced by this task.

annotation.summary: Adds retry, reply/system-prompt editing, editable bans and JSON session persistence to CLI chat. Explicit-filename loading falls through to generation, and retry/edit lack empty-history guards.
